text.tspan: JSON is TEXT. Going out and coming back is not lossless: know what does not survive.
A NEW object, never the one
Hooks on the way out and back:
JSON.stringify(v, replacer, 2) - filter or reshape, and indent
JSON.parse(text, reviver) - rebuild values as they load
A toJSON() method on an object controls its own output.
a class instance → a plain object
The only JSON types are object, array, string,
number, true, false and null. No comments, no
trailing commas, and keys must be in double
quotes, which is why valid JavaScript is not
So JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj)) is a quick deep copy, but only for plain data; use structuredClone() otherwise.
Always wrap JSON.parse in try/catch: bad input throws a SyntaxError, and network responses are not always what you expect.
